verdict.rationale: Trello's own site says it can automate tasks and workflows, and its developer docs note that some Power-Ups automate workflows, so the product does claim a first-party automation capability. Nothing shows how those automations are triggered, whether they run unattended in the background, or whether they support recurring schedules rather than one-off actions. Board and card buttons are user-triggered, and webhooks are developer building blocks, so neither earns credit here. missing for 10: documented triggers/rules that run without user action, background or recurring scheduled execution, depth of the automation feature set, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
